Garlic Butter Herb Chicken Thighs
Line spacing: 1.25
Recipe Overview
A quick, flavorful, and reliable one-pan dinner featuring crispy pan-seared chicken thighs finished in a rich garlic butter and herb sauce.
Prep Time
Cook Time
Total Time
Servings

10 mins
20 mins
30 mins
4

Ingredients
For the Chicken:
4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (or boneless/skinless)
1 tsp salt
1/2 tsp freshly cracked black pepper
1 tsp smoked paprika
1 tsp onion powder
1 tbsp olive oil
For the Garlic Butter Sauce:
3 tbsp unsalted butter
4 cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp fresh rosemary, finely chopped
1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves
1/2 cup chicken broth or dry white wine
1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Instructions
Season the Chicken: Pat chicken thighs completely dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine salt, black pepper, smoked paprika, and onion powder. Season both sides of the chicken evenly.
Sear: Heat olive oil in a large heavy skillet (preferably cast iron) over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down and sear for 6–8 minutes without moving them, until skin is golden brown and crispy.
Flip & Cook: Flip chicken and cook for another 6–8 minutes until nearly cooked through. Transfer chicken to a plate and set aside.
Make Sauce: Reduce skillet heat to medium. Add butter to the pan. Once melted, add minced garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze: Pour in chicken broth (or white wine), scraping up any browned bits stuck to the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Bring to a low simmer for 2 minutes.
Combine & Finish: Return chicken thighs (and juices) to the skillet, skin-side up. Spoon the garlic butter sauce over the top. Simmer for 3–5 minutes until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C).
Garnish & Serve: Remove from heat, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve hot with sauce spooned over top.

Recipe Notes
Internal Temperature: Always verify cooked chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) using an instant-read meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part.
Skin Crispness: Avoid covering the skillet completely while simmering at the end to keep the skin crispy.
Storage: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a pan or oven.
